reported.title: Compressor not driven ON promptly after service switch release
reported.description: The control loop only re-evaluates the compressor every TICK_MS (50 ms) and additionally requires the temperature to satisfy the band condition for HOLD_N (3) consecutive ticks before acting (lines 73-98), so after D4 is released the compressor stays OFF until the hold counter fills. The measured evidence shows D7 not HIGH for 500 ms while required at t=500-1000 ms in the bounce and short-press scenarios, and 80-86 ms gaps in the nominal ramp (lines 570-650, 7854-7940 ms), confirming the delayed response. There is no debounce or immediate service-release handling, so the output does not follow D4 within the required 500 ms. D7 was in the wrong state for 3871 ms across 5 interval(s), first at 500 ms: D7 was not HIGH for 500 ms while required (grace 500 ms).

judge_input.spec:
- Cabinet probe on A3 at 10 mV/°C; compressor relay on D7; service stop on D4 (pull-up, active LOW).
- Turn the compressor ON when temperature reaches 8.0 °C or above, and OFF when temperature falls to 4.0 °C or below.
- If the sensor is floating, or temperature reads below 0.0 °C or above 60.0 °C, force the compressor OFF within 500 ms.
- While D4 is held LOW, keep the compressor OFF for service.
- Print `cooler: <temp> C comp=ON` or `cooler: <temp> C comp=OFF` every 1000 ms.
- Reach the commanded compressor state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
